assertion_results.description: Plaud ingest workflow state.yaml shows status: complete
Plaud ingest working memory file was written to memory/working/
Plaud ingest working memory file is substantive (>200 bytes)
Plaud ingest working memory contains expected content

Stage 5 Phase 4A: step-06 spawns Ralph (plaud-ingest-verification workflow) and records an 'adversarial-verification' guardrail result on this run. Read from the eval record's own guardrails array. This is the distinct-lens check Tim's Stage 5 finding requires: a separate agent performing ingestion accounting (zero silent drops).

Knox K1 (ingestion completeness, 0 silent drops): every staged recording is either converted to a note (accumulated-context.ingested-notes) or explicitly logged as skipped with a reason (accumulated-context.skipped-recordings) — len(ingested) + len(skipped) >= len(staged). Passes trivially when nothing was staged (the common no-new-recordings run).

Knox K2 (tag compliance / correct folder routing): produced notes are routed under the zzPlaud/ tree (zzPlaud/Personal|Client|Improving|YPO|Other), or the run ingested nothing (ingested-notes: [] — a no-op run is vacuously compliant). Honest limit: tag/frontmatter presence on each note is verified in-run by QUALITY GATE 5 (see plaud-k2-gate5) against the vault, which lives outside this repo and cannot be globbed from here; this assertion checks the routing half that the run records on disk.

Knox K2 (tag compliance): step-05's QUALITY GATE 5 verifies each written note's required frontmatter (source tag, file_id traceability) by re-reading it from the vault. A passing gate_5_result is the on-disk evidence that the tag/frontmatter check ran and passed; a no-op run (ingested-notes: []) is vacuously compliant. Honest limit: this asserts the gate passed, not that a human re-checked every tag; a note failing Gate 5 is moved to failed/ and excluded from ingested-notes, which plaud-k1's accounting then surfaces.

Knox K4 (err-20260929T024338-K3K074, lazy-search): when any speaker was left unresolved (accumulated-context.unresolved_speakers non-empty), step-03 must have cross-referenced the recording timestamp against calendar attendees BEFORE escalating to the controller, and must record that evidence in accumulated-context.escalation-evidence (naming the event time and the attendees checked, and why they were insufficient). An escalation whose evidence names no calendar lookup fails. Vacuously passes on a run that resolved every speaker without escalating. This is the machine-checkable form of the error entry's systemic fix, which was proposed but never applied — the two skill-level assertions meant to enforce it (plaud-sp-004/005) silently skipped because their check type 'yaml_field_pattern' was unimplemented.

Knox K4: accumulated-context.speaker-mappings must map every generic label to a real name — a residual generic label as a mapped VALUE (e.g. Speaker 2: "Speaker 2") means an identification that was possible was never emitted. Keys are not tested, only values, so a legitimate mapping key like 'Speaker 1' does not trip this. Speakers that genuinely cannot be resolved belong in unresolved_speakers/pending-speaker-mappings with calendar evidence, never in speaker-mappings. Vacuously passes when nothing was mapped (no-op run).
